Called Didymus; the apostle who said, “My Lord and my God.” Scripture gives no years for his life, so the ring is divided by how much is recorded: 8 records of what he did or what was said to him, one bead each. The last part is tradition and is drawn dashed. Choose a part to read it.
II · THE GOSPELS, IN THE HARMONY’S ORDER
Chosen as one of the Twelve Mark 3:13–19
Sent out with the Twelve; seventh in Matthew’s list Matthew 10:1–5
“Let us also go, that we may die with him” John 11:7–16
“Lord, we know not whither thou goest” John 14:5–7
Absent when Jesus appears: “Except I shall see” John 20:24–25
Eight days later: “My Lord and my God” John 20:26–29
Fishing with Peter when the risen Jesus appears by the sea John 21:1–3
One square for each chapter of the books that name Thomas: 12 verses in 8 chapters. The darker the square, the more verses in it name him. Choose a chapter to read what happens there.
¶ But Thomas, one of the twelve, called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came.
Absent when Jesus appears: “Except I shall see”
Eight days later: “My Lord and my God”
Then said Thomas, which is called Didymus, unto his fellowdisciples, Let us also go, that we may die with him.
John three times adds that Thomas was “called Didymus” (John 11:16; 20:24; 21:2). Thomas in Syriac and Didymus in Greek both mean “twin” (Thurston, 1912). Scripture never says whose twin he was.

CHAPTER III · THE CHURCH IN ACTS

And when they were come in, they went up into an upper room, where abode both Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, Philip, and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon Zelotes, and Judas the brother of James.
He is named sixth among the Eleven in the upper room (Acts 1:13). Acts never names him again.
